image_description: A close-up portrait of a Brown Pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) facing forward against a plain, light blue-grey background. The bird features dark brown/grey plumage on its neck and body, with a pale yellow/cream-colored head and crown. The most prominent feature is the long, massive bill with a visible gular pouch structure at the base, colored in dull orange/yellow tones. The eye is dark and distinct. The image crops the bird at the chest, excluding legs, feet, tail, and full wing span.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, elongated, and possesses the characteristic structural bulge of the gular pouch at the base of the lower mandible. It matches the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill length significantly exceeds the vertical height of the head. The coloration is yellowish-orange, consistent with non-breeding or sub-adult Brown Pelican morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large with prominent pouch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head proportions are large relative to the neck, and the pouch area is structurally defined.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible plumage is dark brown/grey on the neck and body, with a lighter yellowish head, which is accurate for a Brown Pelican.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits heavy barrel-shaped torso of very large proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Although cropped, the visible upper torso appears robust and broad, consistent with the 'barrel-shaped' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The wings are largely out of frame or folded against the body in this portrait crop. The specific contrast of flight feathers cannot be fully verified due to occlusion/cropping.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely outside the frame of the image.
The neck is visible and exhibits the characteristic thickness and slight curvature typical of pelicans when retracted.
The tail is not visible in this close-up shot.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The transition between the hard keratin of the bill and the skin/feathers of the face is slightly indistinct, lacking the crisp anatomical boundary seen in high-resolution wildlife photography.
